title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE CARDBOARD BOAT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Hollis Grant, a mattress delivery man in Birmingham, Alabama.
Every May, his town races boats made of cardboard and duct tape.
For nine years, Hollis watched from the shore, eating a corn dog.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE CORN DOG
segments.quote: I like work: it fascinates me. I can sit and look at it for hours.
segments.author: Jerome K. Jerome
lines: Last May, his wife Denise found him on the shore again.
She grinned and quoted Jerome K. Jerome, the English humorist:
I like work: it fascinates me. I can sit and look at it for hours.
That stung. Hollis tossed the corn dog and signed up for next year.
His crew: Denise, his partner Luis, and Luis's eighty-year-old Aunt Bea.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CASTLE
segments.quote: Truth is ever to be found in simplicity, and not in the multiplicity and confusion of things.
segments.author: Isaac Newton
lines: By Christmas, Hollis had drawn a boat with a cup holder and a horn.
It weighed as much as a refrigerator.
Aunt Bea, a retired bridge engineer, showed him a line from Isaac Newton:
Truth is ever to be found in simplicity, and not in the multiplicity and confusion of things.
So they built a plain, flat box. Hollis mourned the horn.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE POOL TEST
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: In February, they tested it in a neighbor's pool.
It folded like a wet pizza box, and Hollis went down with it.
Shivering in a towel, he read Denise's fridge magnet from Benjamin Franklin:
The things which hurt, instruct.
Every leak was at a seam. So they painted every seam three times.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE COLD GARAGE
segments.quote: If we had no winter, the spring would not be so pleasant.
segments.author: Anne Bradstreet
lines: The garage was freezing. The paint would not dry. Luis wanted to quit.
Denise read a line from Anne Bradstreet, one of America's first writers:
If we had no winter, the spring would not be so pleasant.
So they kept painting in their coats. By April, the boat was shiny and proud.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LEAK
segments.quote: A good laugh is a mighty good thing, and rather too scarce a good thing.
segments.author: Herman Melville
lines: Race day. Halfway across the lake, the water rose over their ankles.
The whole shore laughed. Hollis turned as red as a stop sign.
Then Luis shouted a line from Herman Melville's Moby Dick:
A good laugh is a mighty good thing, and rather too scarce a good thing.
So they laughed too, and paddled harder.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TITANIC AWARD
segments.quote: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive.
segments.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: Ten feet from the finish, the boat folded in half.
They swam it across, Aunt Bea riding on top like a queen.
Dead last. But they won the Titanic Award: a gold toilet plunger.
Dripping wet, Denise quoted Robert Louis Stevenson:
To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive.
Next year's boat is already in the garage.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Get off the shore. Keep it simple. Learn from it. Push through winter. Laugh. Enjoy the trip.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Get off the shore. Keep it simple. Learn. Push through winter. Laugh. Enjoy the trip.
I built a canoe once myself. It makes a lovely flower planter.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
